The store's list of products and how many of each are in stock.

data.issue: Two parts of the store are waiting on each other: the order part and the inventory part.
data.evidence:
Think of it like this: Imagine two people waiting for each other to open a door.
Person A: “I need B to go first.”
Person B: “I need A to go first.”
Nobody moves. Something similar is happening inside this project.

Loop: Order part (src/services/orderService.js) → Inventory part (src/services/inventoryService.js) → Order part (src/services/orderService.js)

What is happening: The order part needs the inventory part to set products aside. The inventory part needs the order part to look up the order. Each one relies on the other, so together they form a loop.

Technical name: Circular dependency

Why it matters: Because these two parts depend on each other, one can start before the other is ready. Later, when the store tries to cancel an unpaid order, it asks for order information that isn't there — and the store can crash with the error `getOrderById is not a function`. That is the exact error this code would produce on that path.

Files: src/services/orderService.js — Creates and manages customer orders.
src/services/inventoryService.js — Manages the products set aside for orders.
src/jobs/expireOrders.js — Cancels unpaid orders and returns their products.

Possible fix: Give both parts a separate place to look up order information. Then neither part has to depend on the other, and the loop disappears.

Technical fix: Move the shared order lookup (`getOrderById`) into its own module that both services import.

Technical detail: orderService.js imports `reserveStock()` from inventoryService.js, and inventoryService.js imports `getOrderById()` back from orderService.js. inventoryService.js destructures that import at load time, so when orderService.js loads first — the normal path via routes/orders.js — it captures `undefined`. The first `releaseStock()` call, made by the order-expiry job in jobs/expireOrders.js, then throws `getOrderById is not a function`.
